transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-09 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Priya Rao, Samir Patel, Lena Martinez, Eric Johnson, Maya Singh

[00:00:00] Priya Rao: ok everybody, thanks for joining, I'll kick off — this is the weekly admin sync, primarily IT/finance/security. I think we've got a packed agenda: SOC2, Okta provisioning, KMS rotation, and vendor renewals. Aim to leave with clear owners and dates.

[00:00:22] Lena Martinez: thanks Priya. quick FYI from finance side, Q4 planning is starting so I need the renewals list sooner rather than later, we have one big vendor up in mid-october.

[00:00:35] Samir Patel: hi — on SOC2, I pulled the last evidence matrix, it's about 70% populated. we still need the SSO diagrams, the RBAC screenshots, and the admin access logs. I can help with log exports but I need to know exactly which time ranges auditors want.

[00:00:52] Maya Singh: legal side — we need to confirm the auditor NDA is in place and whether the auditor needs access to any production PII. please confirm scope so I can redline the contract.

[00:01:10] Eric Johnson: on the KMS side, we did a partial rotation test in staging last month but haven't updated the runbook in the ops repo. there was a small hiccup with the HSM cert chain, so I want to make sure the runbook documents that failover.

[00:01:33] Priya Rao: ok let's go topic by topic. SOC2 first — Samir, can you run through the remaining evidence? and Lena, after that we can mark what finance needs.

[00:01:48] Samir Patel: sure. remaining items: SSO configuration screenshots (Okta org settings, SCIM mapping), admin user lists with last-login, audit log exports from the platform (authn, authz changes), encryption key management policy artifacts, and change control tickets for infra config. We also need confirmation of retention windows for logs.

[00:02:15] Lena Martinez: retention windows — finance cares about cost, are we going to keep 12 months or longer? there was discussion about 18 months but that bumps storage. what's the default?

[00:02:29] Eric Johnson: current default is 12 months in hot storage, older rolled to cold for three more years. but we haven't formalized policy docs. that's on me to update.

[00:02:40] Priya Rao: action: Eric updates the log retention doc and posts link. Samir will pull logs for the auditor. Lena will indicate preferred retention for budgeting.

[00:02:55] Samir Patel: one note — the log export tool trims some fields; for SOC2 we should provide redacted full events, sometimes the transcriber removes fields so I need to do a manual review. also occasional typos in the auto transcripts, I saw 'KV cache' mis-typed as 'K-V cash' in earlier notes.

[00:03:18] Maya Singh: haha ok noted, make sure the export is redacted. also we need to confirm whether the auditors get oltp or readonly accounts, and the access window. legal typically wants a limited-time read-only account with 2FA and IP allowlist.

[00:03:37] Priya Rao: agreed. Samir — can you propose an auditor access plan? including read-only, just-in-time admin if needed, and IP allowlist?

[00:03:46] Samir Patel: yes, I'll draft that. thinking JIT roles via Okta, ephemeral admin sessions, and we can use SCIM to provision auditor accounts. note: our Okta SCIM automation is flakey for groups right now.

[00:04:05] Eric Johnson: about Okta — we had a ticket to fix SCIM group mapping that is still open. it's on my backlog but I can prioritize. the third-party SCIM connector needs an update, and there was a mismatch between the group attribute and the application mapping.

[00:04:26] Priya Rao: prioritize it please — it affects provisioning for a few teams and the auditor onboarding. Lena, does finance rely on any of these automations for billing or license counting?

[00:04:36] Lena Martinez: yes, we use the Okta license counts to reconcile vendor seats monthly. if SCIM is wrong it shows extra seats and we overpay. please fix.

[00:04:44] Samir Patel: quick aside — we had an inbound question about encryption: do we rotate CMKs monthly or quarterly? currently quarterly, but the auditor prefers documented cadence and evidence of last rotation.

[00:04:59] Eric Johnson: we rotate quarterly for root keys, and we rotate data keys more often when suspicious activity. I will add rotation dates to the KMS dashboard. also update the runbook with the HSM failover steps I mentioned.

[00:05:15] Maya Singh: for the auditor contract, please send me the details of the scope and the minimal necessary data. I will flag anything that needs PCI/PII redaction or extra controls.

[00:05:27] Priya Rao: sounds good. now vendor renewals: Lena, what's the one up in mid-Oct?

[00:05:33] Lena Martinez: it's our monitoring vendor — contract auto-renews Oct 18 if we don't provide a renewal notice. renewal is about $95k annually; we might want to shop that or negotiate. also the identity provider renewal is in December.

[00:05:45] Priya Rao: ok we should add both to the renewal calendar and align potential cost savings. Samir, does the monitoring vendor need any special access for the SOC2 work?

[00:05:53] Samir Patel: they usually need readonly access to metrics and some agent logs. we can create a scoped account. but we need to capture the vendor's SOC2 or equivalent — if they have it, that reduces our evidence burden.

[00:06:10] Lena Martinez: I'll add vendor SOC2 status to the spreadsheet.

[00:06:15] Eric Johnson: another ops item — we should standardize runbook locations and naming. auditors asked for 'where is change control evidence' and we had a few scattered docs. I'm proposing ops/runbooks/kms-rotation.md etc.

[00:06:32] Priya Rao: yes standardization is key. Eric, please consolidate and PR. Samir, once you have log exports, we'll redact and upload to the evidence folder.

[00:06:45] Samir Patel: timeline — I can get initial exports and a list of missing items by end of this week. full curated evidence by next Monday.

[00:06:53] Maya Singh: I'll review the auditor NDA by Thursday and flag anything unusual. also do we want to ask auditors for a SOC2 maturity questionnaire before they arrive? it can speed up their scoping.

[00:07:05] Priya Rao: yes, good idea. Samir, add that to your tasks.

[00:07:12] Samir Patel: noted. will request the maturity questionnaire.

[00:07:18] Lena Martinez: finance question: for the auditor travel, do we reimburse? Usually SOC auditors ask for some onsite access, but this round might be remote. if onsite, what's policy on travel spend?

[00:07:30] Maya Singh: legal will handle travel permissions; finance will process reimbursements per policy. but let's try remote first to limit cost.

[00:07:40] Eric Johnson: technical deep-dive note — our private deployment docs need a quick update: network diagrams referenced in SOC2 were out of date. I have a draft but need an owner to vet.

[00:07:53] Priya Rao: Samir and Eric will own network diagram updates. Samir will validate security annotations, Eric will update the topology and label subnets.

[00:08:03] Samir Patel: small transcription note — sometimes Fireflies transcribes 'private deploy' as 'private deploye', so watch for typos in artifacts.

[00:08:10] Priya Rao: thanks. moving to runbook specifics: Eric, what's the HSM cert chain hiccup you referred to?

[00:08:17] Eric Johnson: when we rotated staging keys, one of the HSM peers didn't pick up the new cert, it fell back to previous chain and alerts fired. The fix was to reload the HSM agent process and flush the local keystore. I want that sequence documented and tested.

[00:08:34] Priya Rao: ok that's an action for Eric. also create a postmortem template entry so auditors can see we tracked the incident.

[00:08:42] Eric Johnson: will do.

[00:08:45] Priya Rao: any blockers we should call out?

[00:08:48] Lena Martinez: budget — need headcount approvals for the assessor if we hire a third-party to compress the audit window. estimate $25-40k. I'll create a quick ask for leadership.

[00:09:00] Maya Singh: legal needs to review scope before we engage a third party. please include preliminary scope in the ask.

[00:09:07] Priya Rao: agreed. Lena to draft ask, include Samir's list of required artifacts and timeframe, Maya will review.

[00:09:15] Samir Patel: last note — export retention windows: confirm data retention for logs and backups; auditors will ask for deletion policies.

[00:09:25] Eric Johnson: I'll formalize retention policy text and link to storage cost estimate.

[00:09:32] Priya Rao: great. let's recap owners and dates.

[00:09:35] Recap:
- Priya: coordinate evidence folder and finalize meeting cadence (owner of follow-ups)
- Samir: draft auditor access plan, pull and redact logs, request maturity questionnaire (due 2026-09-15)
- Eric: update KMS rotation runbook, HSM failover steps, and log retention doc (due 2026-09-16)
- Lena: compile vendor renewal calendar, cost estimates, and budget ask (due 2026-09-16)
- Maya: review NDA and auditor scope, provide comments (due 2026-09-14)

[00:10:10] Priya Rao: ok thanks everyone. I'll send the SOC2 evidence spreadsheet link after this call and book the auditor prep walkthrough for next week. any final comments?

[00:10:22] Samir Patel: none from me.

[00:10:24] Lena Martinez: nope.

[00:10:25] Maya Singh: all good.

[00:10:26] Eric Johnson: done.

[00:10:28] Priya Rao: meeting adjourned.

End transcript. Note: transcription contains minor mis-hearings and occasional auto-caption errors (e.g., Okto for Okta, K-V cash for KV cache).
